(&#8220;Epsilon&#8221;), Mitsui and Chief Oil &amp; Gas LLC (&#8220;Chief&#8221;), we have agreed to provide the following services in our Marcellus Shale region for our proportionate share (based on our ownership interest in the applicable systems) of the fees and obligations outlined below: </font></p><div align="left"><table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:95.46%;margin-left:4.54%;margin-right:0%"><tr><td valign="top" style="width:4.54%;white-space:nowrap"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;</font></p></td><td valign="top" style="width:95.46%;"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"></font><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Gathering and Compression Services</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">. In systems operated by Appalachia Midstream, we gather and compress natural gas in exchange for fees per million British thermal units (&#8220;MMBtu&#8221;) of natural gas gathered and per MMBtu of natural gas compressed. Our responsibility for the cost of the lost gas may subject us to direct commodity price risk. </font></p></td></tr></table></div><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Niobrara Shale Region.</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">&#160;&#160;Under our gas gathering and processing agreements with Chesapeake and RKI Exploration</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> &amp; Production, LLC (&#8220;RKI&#8221;), we have agreed to provide the following services for the fees and obligations outlined below: </font></p><div align="left"><table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; We will gather, compress, dehydrate and process natural gas and liquids within the Niobrara region in exchange for a cost of service based fee for natural gas and liquids gathered on our gathering systems and for natural gas and liquids processed at our proposed processing facility. There is no cap on these fee adjustments. </font></p></td></tr></table></div><div align="left"><table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:95.46%;margin-left:4.54%;margin-right:0%"><tr><td valign="top" style="width:4.54%;white-space:nowrap"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;</font></p></td><td valign="top" style="width:95.46%;"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"></font><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Well Connections</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">.&#160;&#160;Subject to required notice by Chesapeake and RKI, we will have the option to connect new operated wells within our Niobrara region acreage dedications as requested by our producer customers. Subject to certain conditions specified in the gas gathering agreements, if we elect to connect a new well to our gathering systems, we are generally required to connect the new wells within specified timelines subject to penalties for delayed connections up to a specified cap, and the potential for a well pad release from the producer customer&#8217;s acreage dedication in certain circumstances. </font></p></td></tr></table></div><div align="left"><table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:95.46%;margin-left:4.54%;margin-right:0%"><tr><td valign="top" style="width:4.54%;white-space:nowrap"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;</font></p></td><td valign="top" style="width:95.46%;"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"></font><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Fuel and Lost and Unaccounted For Gas</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">. We have agreed with Chesapeake and RKI to a cap on fuel and lost and unaccounted for gas on our systems with respect to the producers&#8217; volumes. The cap is based on a percentage per deemed compression stage and a percentage for lost and unaccounted for gas. We and our producer customers determine adjustments to fees for the gathering systems in the region with our producer customers based on the factors specified in the gas gathering agreement, including, but not limited to, differences between our actual capital expenditures, compression expenses and revenues as of the redetermination date and the scheduled estimates of these amounts for the period ending June&#160;30, 2019, referred to as the redetermination period, made as of September&#160;30, 2009. The annual upward or downward fee adjustment for the Mid-Continent region is capped at 15 percent of the then current fees at the time of redetermination. </font></p></td></tr></table></div><div align="left"><table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:95.46%;margin-left:4.54%;margin-right:0%"><tr><td valign="top" style="width:4.54%;white-space:nowrap"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;</font></p></td><td valign="top" style="width:95.46%;"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"></font><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Well Connection Requirement.&#160;&#160;</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Subject to required notice by our producer customers and certain exceptions, we have generally agreed to use our commercially reasonable efforts to connect new operated drilling pads and new operated wells in our Mid-Continent region acreage dedications as requested by our producer customers through June&#160;30, 2019. </font></p></td></tr></table></div><div align="left"><table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:95.46%;margin-left:4.54%;margin-right:0%"><tr><td valign="top" style="width:4.54%;white-space:nowrap"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;</font></p></td><td valign="top" style="width:95.46%;"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"></font><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Fuel and Lost and Unaccounted For Gas.&#160;&#160;</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We have agreed with our producer customers on caps on fuel and lost and unaccounted for gas on our systems, both on an individual basis and an aggregate basis, with respect to our producer customers volumes. These caps do not apply to certain of our gathering systems due to their historic performance relative to the caps. These systems are reviewed annually to determine whether changes have occurred that would make them suitable for inclusion. If we exceed a permitted cap in any covered period, we may incur significant expenses to replace the natural gas used as fuel or lost or unaccounted for in excess of such cap based on then current natural gas prices. Accordingly, this replacement obligation will subject us to direct commodity price risk. </font></p></td></tr></table></div><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">As part of the CMO Acquisition, we acquired a 33.33</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> percent equity interest in Ranch Westex JV LLC, which we own jointly with Regency Energy Partners, LP and Anadarko Pecos Midstream LLC. Under a gas processing agreement with Chesapeake and Anadarko, Ranch Westex JV LLC provides natural gas processing services under a cost of service fee arrangement. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">All Regions.</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">&#160;&#160;If one of th</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">e counterparties these the gas gathering and processing agreements sells, transfers or otherwise disposes of properties within the our acreage dedications to a third party, it does so subject to the terms of the gas gathering and processing agreements, including our dedication, and it will be required to cause the third party to acknowledge and take assignment of the counterparty&#8217;s obligations under the existing gas gathering and processing agreements with us, subject to our consent. Our producer customers&#8217; dedication of the natural gas produced from applicable properties under our gas gathering and processing agreements will run with the land in order to bind successors to the producer customers&#8217; interest, as well as any interests in the dedicated properties subsequently acquired by the producer customer.</font><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">48</font></p>

<div style="width:100%;"><hr style="page-break-after:always"></div><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Other Arrangements </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">On June&#160;15, 2012, in connection with the closing of the first portion of the acquisition by the GIP II Entities of Chesapeake&#8217;s ownership interest in us</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> (the &#8220;GIP Acquisition&#8221;), we entered into a letter agreement with Chesapeake regarding the terms on which Chesapeake provides certain transition services to us and our general partner.&#160;Among other things, the letter agreement provided for the continuation of our services agreement with Chesapeake until December&#160;31, 2013. On June&#160;29, 2012, we entered into an amendment to the letter agreement amending certain terms relating to the insurance coverage to be provided under our services agreement. On December&#160;20, 2012, in connection with the CMO Acquisition, we entered into an amendment to the letter agreement amending certain terms relating primarily to the extension of transition services for technology related services through March 2014 and through June 2014 for certain field communication support services. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">How We Evaluate Our Operations </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Our management relies on certain financial and operational metrics to analyze our performance. These metrics are significant factors in assessing our operating results and profitability and include (i)&#160;throughput volumes, (ii)&#160;revenues, (iii)&#160;operating expenses,</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> (iv) segment operating income, (v)&#160;Adjusted EBITDA and (vi)&#160;distributable cash flow. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Throughput Volumes </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Our management analyzes our performance based on the aggregate amount of throughput volumes on our gathering systems in our operating regions in order to maintain or increase throughput volumes on our gathering systems as a whole. Our success in connecting additional wells is impacted by successful drilling activity on the acreage dedicated to our systems, our ability to secure volumes from new wells drilled on non-dedicated acreage, our ability to attract natural gas and liquids volumes currently gathered </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">by our competitors and our ability to cost-effectively construct new infrastructure to connect new wells. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Revenues </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Our revenues are driven primarily by our contractual terms with our customers and the actual volumes of natural gas we gather, treat,</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> compress and process. Our revenues will be supported by the minimum volume commitments contained in our gas gathering agreements with Chesapeake and Total in the case of our Barnett Shale and Chesapeake in the case of our Haynesville Shale as well as fee redetermination and cost of service provisions in our other regions. We contract with producers to gather or process natural gas or liquids from individual wells located near our gathering systems or processing facilities. We connect wells to gathering pipelines through which natural gas is compressed and may be delivered to a treating facility, processing plant or an intrastate or interstate pipeline for delivery to market. We treat natural gas and liquids that we gather to the extent necessary to meet required specifications of third-party takeaway pipelines. For the years ended December&#160;31, 2013, 2012 and 2011, Chesapeake accounted for approximately 74 percent, 81 percent and 84 percent, respectively, of the natural gas volumes on our gathering systems and 84 percent, 81 percent and 83 percent, respectively, of our revenues.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Partnership&#8217;s revenues exclude revenue attributable to the Partnership&#8217;s equity investments as those revenues are accounted for as part of the Partnership&#8217;s investments in unconsolidated affiliates.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Our revenues are also impacted by other aspects of our contractual agreements, including rate redetermination, cost of service and other contractual provisions and our management constantly evaluates capital spending and its impact on future revenue generation. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.53%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Operating Expenses </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Our management seeks to maximize the profitability of our operations by minimizing operating expenses without compromising environmental protection and employee safety. Operating expenses are comprised primarily of field operating costs (which include labor, treating and chemicals, and measurements services among other items), compression expense, ad valorem and taxes and other operating costs, some of which are independent of the volumes that flow through our sys</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">tems but fluctuate depending on the scale of our operations during a specific period. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.53%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold;;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Segment Operating Income</font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.17%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.17%">Prior to the CMO Acquisition, our operations were organized into a single business segment. As a result of the CMO Acquisition, we added assets in three new operating regions. Effective January 1, 2013, our chief operating decision </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">49</font></p>

<div style="width:100%;"><hr style="page-break-after:always"></div><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">maker began to measure performance and allocate resources based on geographic segments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our operations are divided into eight operating segments: Barnett Shale, Eagle Ford Shale, Haynesville Shale, Marcellus Shale, Niobrara Shale, Utica Shale, Mid-Continent and Corporate.</font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.53%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Adjusted EBITDA and Distributable Cash Flow </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">We define Adjusted EBITDA as net income (loss) before income tax expense (benefit), interest expense, depreciation and amortization expense and certain other items management believes effect the comparability of operating results. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">We define distributable cash flow as Adjusted EBITDA, plus interest income, less cash paid for interest expense, maintenance capital expenditures and income taxes. Distributable cash flow does not reflect changes in working capital balances. Distributable cash flow and Adjusted EBITDA are not presentations made in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;). </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Adjusted EBITDA and distributable cash flow are non-GAAP supplemental financial measures that management and external users of our consolidated financial statements, such as industry analysts, investors, lenders and rating agencies, may use to assess: </font></p><div align="left"><table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:95.46%;margin-left:4.54%;margin-right:0%"><tr><td valign="top" style="width:4.54%;white-space:nowrap"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;</font></p></td><td valign="top" style="width:95.46%;"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">our operating </font><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">performance</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> as compared to other publicly traded partnerships in the midstream energy industry, without regard to historical cost basis, or in the case of Adjusted EBITDA, financing methods; </font></p></td></tr></table></div><div align="left"><table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:95.46%;margin-left:4.54%;margin-right:0%"><tr><td valign="top" style="width:4.54%;white-space:nowrap"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;</font></p></td><td valign="top" style="width:95.46%;"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">our ability to incur and service debt and fund capital expenditures; </font></p></td></tr></table></div><div align="left"><table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:95.46%;margin-left:4.54%;margin-right:0%"><tr><td valign="top" style="width:4.54%;white-space:nowrap"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;</font></p></td><td valign="top" style="width:95.46%;"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">the ability of our </font><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">assets</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> to generate sufficient cash flow to make distributions to our unitholders; and </font></p></td></tr></table></div><div align="left"><table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:95.46%;margin-left:4.54%;margin-right:0%"><tr><td valign="top" style="width:4.54%;white-space:nowrap"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;</font></p></td><td valign="top" style="width:95.46%;"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">the viability of </font><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">acquisitions</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> and other capital expenditure projects and the returns on investment of various investment opportunities. </font></p></td></tr></table></div><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.53%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reconciliation to GAAP measures </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">We believe that the presentation of Adjusted EBITDA and distributable cash flow provides useful information to investors in assessing our financial condition and results of operations. Adjusted EBITDA and distributable cash flow are presented because they are h</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">elpful to management, industry analysts, investors, lenders and rating agencies and may be used to assess the financial performance and operating results of our fundamental business activities. The GAAP measures most directly comparable to Adjusted EBITDA and distributable cash flow are net income and net cash provided by operating activities. Our non-GAAP financial measures of Adjusted EBITDA and distributable cash flow should not be considered as an alternative to GAAP net income or net cash provided by operating activities. Each of Adjusted EBITDA and distributable cash flow has important limitations as an analytical tool because it excludes some but not all items that affect net income and net cash provided by operating activities. You should not consider either Adjusted EBITDA or distributable cash flow in isolation or as a substitute for analysis of our results as reported under GAAP. Because Adjusted EBITDA and distributable cash flow may be defined differently by other companies in our industry, our definitions of Adjusted EBITDA and distributable cash flow may not be comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies, thereby diminishing their utility. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The following table presents a reconciliation of the non-GAAP financial measures of Adjusted EBITDA and distributable cash flow to the GAAP financial measures of net income and net cash provided by operating activities: </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;"><font style="font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</font></p><div>

vertical-align:top">(2)</sup></font><font style="font-size:7.5pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</font></p></td><td valign="top" style="width:98.87%;"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-size:7.5pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:7.5pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%; <div style="width:100%;"><hr style="page-break-after:always"></div><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.53%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Barnett Shale </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Revenues</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">. For the years ended December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> and 2012, revenues totaled $433.7 million and $395.5 million, respectively. The increase was primarily the result of increasing volumes under our minimum volume commitment and the full year impact of the five cents per mcf fee redetermination which was effective on July 1, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;Total revenue for 2013 includes $64.9 million of revenues associated with the contractual minimum volume commitment.&nbsp;&nbsp;The minimum volume revenue offset a decrease in throughput of 12.8 percent due to decreased drilling activity by Chesapeake in 2013. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Operating Expenses</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">.&#160;&#160;For the years ended December&#160;31, 2013 and 2</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">012, operating expenses were $96.9 million, or $0.25 per Mcf, compared to $101.7 million, or $0.23 per Mcf, respectively. Total operating expenses decreased 4.7% consistent with the decrease in throughput. The most significant operating expenses in the Barnett Shale region are compression costs. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Depreciation and Amortization Expenses</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">. For the years ended </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">December&#160;31, 2013 and 2012, depreciation expenses were $97.9 million and $93.3 million, respectively. The increase was due to capital expenditures made in this region during 2013 and 2012. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.53%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Eagle Ford Shale </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">We acquired the Eagle Ford Shale assets in December 2012. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Revenues.</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%"> For the year ended December 31, 2013, revenues in the Eagle Ford totaled $278.3 million and were primarily attributable to the amount of throughput on our gathering systems and the rates charged for gathering such throughput.&nbsp;&nbsp;We inves</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ted $316.0 million of capital in this region in 2013 and as a result, we expect increased revenues in 2014.</font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Operating Expenses.</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%"> For the year ended December 31, 2013, operating expenses totaled $59.1 million, or $0.62 per Mcf. The most significant operating</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> expenses in this region are employee compensation and compression costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;We expect our operating expenses to increase in this region in 2014 if Chesapeake increases its drilling activity. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Depreciation and Amortization Expenses</font><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">.</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> Depreciation and amortization expense for the year ended December 31, 2013, was $51.4 million and related almost entirely to depreciation of our operating assets in the region.</font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.53%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Haynesville Shale </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Revenues</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">. For the years ended December&#160;31, </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2013 and 2012, revenues were $119.2 million and $68.2 million, respectively. An overall increase in throughput of 76.5 percent resulted from production from the Mansfield gathering system acquired in December 2012, offset by a volume decrease for the Springridge gathering system of 16.1 percent.&nbsp;&nbsp;Haynesville revenues were positively impacted by an annual rate escalation of 2.5 percent and rate redetermination of 15 percent on the Springridge gathering system, both effective January 1, 2013. Additionally, we have contractual minimum volume commitments from Chesapeake in the Haynesville Shale. Throughput for each of the years ended December 31, 2013 and 2012 was above the minimum volume commitment levels. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Operating Expenses</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">. For the years ended December&#160;31, 2013 and 2012, operating expenses we</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">re $41.2 million and $15.6 million, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;All of our operating expenses in this region increased significantly as a result of the acquisition of the Mansfield gathering system in December 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;Operating expenses per Mcf increased primarily due to the need for additional treating services for the natural gas gathered in our Mansfield gathering system. We continue to evaluate reductions in our operating costs in this dry gas region to address the decrease in throughput caused by the low natural gas price environment. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.53%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Marcellus Shale </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">On September 4, 2013, we sold Mid-Atlantic Gas Services, L.L.C. (&#8220;Mid-Atlantic&#8221;) to Chesapeake for net proceeds of $32.9 million. Mid-Atlantic was acquired in December 2012 and consisted of midstream assets in the Marcellus region.&nbsp;&nbsp;These assets were not part of our equity method investment in Appalachia Midstream. The net proceeds equaled our basis in the assets; thus, no gain or loss was recognized as a result of the sale.</font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">54</font></p>

<div style="width:100%;"><hr style="page-break-after:always"></div><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The large </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">majority of our assets in the Marcellus Shale are accounted for as equity investments and included in Income from Unconsolidated Affiliates. See further discussion below under &#8220;Income from Unconsolidated Affiliates&#8221; in this section of Marcellus Shale results of operations. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Income from unconsolidated affiliates. </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On December&#160;29, 2011, we acquired all of the issued and outstanding equity interest in Appalachia Midstream, which owns an approximate average 47 percent interest in 10 gas gathering systems in the Marcellus Shale in Pennsylvania and West Virginia. The remaining average 53 percent interests in these assets are owned primarily by Statoil, Anadarko, Epsilon and Mitsui. Income from unconsolidated affiliates was $133.0 million and $67.6 million reflecting activity for the years ended December&#160;31, 2013 and 2012, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenues (net to our interest) for the years ended December 31, 2013 and 2012 were $234.8 million and $140.5 million, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;The net increase was due to throughput growth and increased construction activity in the Marcellus region where we invested $289.7 million of capital in 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Operating expenses on a per unit basis for the years ended December 31, 2013 and 2012 were $0.10 Mcf and $0.06 Mcf, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;The increase in operating expenses is consistent with the increase in revenues in the Marcellus region.&nbsp;&nbsp;The margin for these assets is strong as a result of lower operating expenses than in many other regions of the United States. These lower operating expenses are primarily due to high reservoir pressures that reduce the need for compression in the transportation of commodities.&nbsp;&nbsp;We expect our margin in the Marcellus Shale to remain strong; however, we could experience a slight decrease in our margin over time as the need for additional compression increases. The following table summarizes the results of the Appalachia Midstream assets (net to our interest) for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013. </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;"><font style="font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</font></p><div>

</table></div><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.53%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Niobrara Shale </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">We acquired </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">our ownership interest in the Niobrara Shale assets in December 2012 and own that interest through our 50 percent ownership interest in Jackalope Gas Gathering, L.L.C., in which Crestwood Niobrara LLC owns the remaining 50 percent interest.&#160;Because we operate the assets and have contractual discretion to make operating decisions for the assets, we are deemed to control the assets and thus, we consolidated 100 percent of the assets and results of operation in our financial results. We present the noncontrolling interest for these assets in Noncontrolling Interests on the condensed consolidated balance sheet and in Net Income Attributable to Noncontrolling Interests on the condensed consolidated statement of operations.</font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Revenues.</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">&nbsp;&nbsp;For the year ended December 31, 2013, revenues in the </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Niobrara Shale region were $15.1 million and were primarily attributable to the amount of throughput on our gathering systems and the rates charged for gathering such throughput.&nbsp;&nbsp;We continue to invest significant capital in this region that is expected to drive volume growth in future periods.</font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Operating Expenses.</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%"> For the year ended December 31, 2013, operating expenses in the Niobrara Shale region were $9.1 million. Expenses are expected to increase significantly in 2014 as construction activity increases </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">and we prepare to provide additional gathering and processing services in this region in future periods. The most significant expenses in this region are employee compensation and compression costs. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.53%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Utica Shale </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">In the CMO Acquisition, we acquired a 100 percent ownership interest in four natural gas gathering systems, a 66 percent operating interest in the Cardinal Joint Venture and a 49 percent interest in the UEO Joint Venture. Because we operate the four wholly-owned natural gas gathering systems and Ca</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">rdinal Joint Venture and have contractual discretion to make operating decisions for the Cardinal Joint Venture, we are deemed to control the assets and, as a result, we consolidate 100 percent of the assets and results of operations in our financial results and reflect the ownership of the other interest owners through a noncontrolling interest in the income and equity of the investment. The UEO Joint Venture is accounted for as an equity investment because the power to direct the activities which are most significant to the UEO Joint Venture&#8217;s economic performance is shared between us and the other equity holders.</font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">55</font></p>

<div style="width:100%;"><hr style="page-break-after:always"></div><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Revenues.</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">&nbsp;&nbsp;For the year ended December 31, 2013, revenues in the Utica Shale region were $44.1 million and were primarily attributable to the am</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ount of throughput and rates charged for such throughput on our gathering systems and gathering systems included in the Cardinal Joint Venture.&nbsp;&nbsp;We continue to invest significant capital in this region that is expected to drive volume and revenue growth in future periods.</font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Operating expenses.</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">&nbsp;&nbsp;For the year ended December 31, 2013, operating expenses in the Utica Shale region were $19.1 million. The increase in operating expenses resulted from additional technical resources to support the assets acquired in 2012. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">General and Administrative Expense.</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">&#160;&#160;For the years ended December&#160;31, 2013 and 2012, general </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">and administrative expenses were $104.3 million and $67.6 million, respectively, representing an increase of 54.3 percent. This increase is primarily attributable to additional overhead expenses resulting from the increased scale of our operations following the CMO Acquisition, additional expense from equity-based, long-term incentive compensation influenced by the increase in our unit price, as well as transition costs as we developed an independent back office infrastructure. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Interest Expense. </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Interest e</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">xpense for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013 was $116.8 million, which was net of $43.9 million of capitalized interest. Interest expense was $64.7 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2012, which was net of $14.6 million of capitalized interest. The increase is related to interest expense on the 2023 Notes, issued in December 2012 and Additional Notes, issued August 2013. We also incurred interest expenses on borrowings under our revolving credit facility and our outstanding senior notes. Interest expense also includes commitment fees on the unused portion of our credit facility and amortization of debt issuance costs. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Income Tax Expense. </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Income tax expense for the years ended December&#160;31, 2013 and 2012 was $</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">5.2 million and $3.2 million, respectively, and was attributable to franchise taxes in the state of Texas. We and our subsidiaries are pass-through entities for federal income tax purposes. For these entities, all income, expenses, gains, losses and tax credits generated flow through to their owners and, accordingly, do not result in a provision for income taxes in the financial statements, other than Texas franchise tax. </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">56</font></p>

</table></div><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.53%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Niobrara Shale </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">We acquired a</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> 50 percent ownership interest in the Niobrara Shale assets in December 2012.&#160;Because we operate the assets and have contractual discretion to make operating decisions for the assets, we are deemed to control the assets and thus, we consolidated 100 percent of the assets and results of operation in our financial results. We present the noncontrolling interest for these assets in Noncontrolling Interests on the condensed consolidated balance sheet and in Net Income Attributable to Noncontrolling Interests on the condensed consolidated statement of operations. For the twelve-day period from closing the CMO Acquisition on December&#160;20, 2012 through December&#160;31, 2012, revenues and operating expenses in the Niobrara Shale were $0.1 million and $0.1 million, respectively. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.53%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Utica Shale </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">In the CMO Acquisition, we acquired a 100 percent ownership interest in four natural gas gathering systems, a 66 percent operating interest in the Cardinal Joint Venture and a 49 percent interest in the UEO Joint Venture. Because we operate the four wholly-owned natu</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ral gas gathering systems and Cardinal Joint Venture and have contractual discretion to make operating decisions for the Cardinal Joint Venture, we are deemed to control the assets and thus, we consolidated 100 percent of the assets and results of operations in our financial results and reflect the ownership of the other interest owners through a noncontrolling interest in the income and equity of the investment. The UEO Joint Venture is accounted for as an equity investment because the power to direct the activities which are most significant to the UEO Joint Venture&#8217;s economic performance is shared between us and the other equity holders. For the twelve-day period from closing the CMO Acquisition on December&#160;20, 2012 through December&#160;31, 2012, revenues and operating expenses in the Utica Shale were $0.4 million and $0.2 million, respectively. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.53%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Mid-Continent </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Revenues</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">.&#160;&#160;For the years ended December&#160;31, 2012 and 2011, revenues were $136.3 million and $111.0 million, respectively. This increase was due to incr</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">eased throughput of 2.5 percent as drilling activity increased in this liquids-rich region, a 2.5 percent annual fee escalation and a 15 percent fee increase due to annual contractual fee redetermination. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Operating Expenses</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">.&#160;&#160;For the years ended December&#160;</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">31, 2012 and 2011, operating expenses were $53.0 million and $47.7 million, respectively. Operating expenses increased due to added compression to support additional throughput. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.53%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Corporate </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Operating Expenses</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">.&#160;&#160;For the years ended December&#160;31, 2012 and 201</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">1, operating expenses were $25.3 million and $17.0 million, respectively. The increase in operating expenses resulted from additional technical resources to support the assets we acquired in 2011. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">General and Administrative Expense.</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">&#160;&#160;For the years ended D</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ecember&#160;31, 2012 and 2011, general and administrative expenses were $67.6 million and $40.4 million, respectively, representing an increase of 67.3 percent. This increase is primarily attributable to additional overhead expenses resulting from the increased scale of our operations, additional expense from equity-based, long-term incentive compensation influenced by the recent increase in our unit </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">59</font></p>

<div style="width:100%;"><hr style="page-break-after:always"></div><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">price, one-time transition costs as we develop an independent back office infrastructure and $15.0 million of transaction costs related to the CMO Acquisition. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Interest Expense.</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">&#160;&#160;Interest expense for the year ended December&#160;31, 2012 was $64.7 million, which was net of $14.6 million of capitalized interest. Interest expense was $14.9 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2011, which was net of $9.5 million of capitalized interes</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">t. The increase is related to interest expense on the $750 million of senior notes issued in January 2012 and $1.4 billion of senior notes issued in December 2012. We incurred interest expenses on borrowings under our revolving credit facility and our senior notes issued in April 2011. Interest expense also includes commitment fees on the unused portion of our credit facility and amortization of debt issuance costs. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Income Tax Expense.</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">&#160;&#160;Income tax expense for the years ended December&#160;31, 2012 and 2011 was </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">$3.2 million and $3.3 million, respectively, and was attributable to franchise taxes in the state of Texas. The Partnership and its subsidiaries are pass-through entities for federal income tax purposes. For these entities, all income, expenses, gains, losses and tax credits generated flow through to their owners and, accordingly, do not result in a provision for income taxes in the financial statements, other than Texas Franchise Tax. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Liquidity and Capital Resources </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Our ability to finance operations and fund capital expenditures will largely depend on our ability to generate sufficient cash flow to cover these expenses as well as the availability of borrowings under our revolving credit facility and our access to the capital markets. Our ability to genera</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">te cash flow is subject to a number of factors, some of which are beyond our control. See </font><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Risk Factors </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">in Item&#160;1A of this annual report. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Historically, our sources of liquidity included cash generated from operations and borrowings under our revolving credit facility. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Working Capital (Deficit)</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">.&#160;&#160;Working capital, defined as the amount by which current assets exceed current liabilities, is an indication of liquidity and the potential need for short-term funding. As of December&#160;31, 2013 and 2012, we had worki</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ng capital deficits of $48.5 million and $39.5 million, respectively, due to our capital intensive business that requires significant investment in new midstream operating assets and to maintain and improve existing facilities. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Cash Flows. </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Net cash provid</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ed by (used in) operating activities, investing activities and financing activities of the Partnership for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013 and 2012 were as follows: </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;"><font style="font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</font></p><div>

The amended and restated revolving credit facility matures in May 2018 and includes aggregate revolving commitments of $1.75 billion, including a sub-limit of $100 million for same-day swing line advances and a sub-limit of $200 million for letters of credit. In addition, the revolving credit facility&#8217;s accordion feature allows us to increase the available borrowing capacity under the facility up to $2.0 billion, subject to the satisfaction of certain conditions, including the identification of lenders or proposed lenders that agree to satisfy the increased commitment amounts under the revolving credit facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December&#160;31, 2013, we had approximately $343.5 million of borrowings outstanding under our revolving credit facility. As of December&#160;31, 2012, there were no borrowings outstanding. </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Borrowings under the revolving credit facility are available to fund working capital, finance capital expenditures and acquisitions, provide for the issuance of letters of credit and for general partnership purposes. The revolving credit facility is secured by all of our assets, and loans thereunder (other than swing line loans) bear interest at our option at either (i)&#160;</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">the greater of (a)&#160;the reference rate of Wells Fargo Bank, NA, (b)&#160;the federal funds effective rate plus 0.50 percent or (c)&#160;the Eurodollar rate which is based on the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR), plus 1.00 percent, each of which is subject to a margin that varies from 0.50 percent to 1.50 percent per annum, according to our leverage ratio (as defined in the agreement), or (ii)&#160;the Eurodollar rate plus a margin that varies from 1.50 percent to 2.50 percent per annum, according to our leverage ratio. If we reach investment grade status, we will have the option to release the security under the credit facility and amounts borrowed will bear interest under a specified ratings-based pricing grid. The unused portion of the credit facility is subject to commitment fees of (a)&#160;0.25 percent to 0.375 percent per annum while we are subject to the leverage-based pricing grid, according to our leverage ratio and (b)&#160;0.15 percent to 0.30 percent per annum while we are subject to the ratings-based pricing grid, according to our senior unsecured long-term debt ratings. </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Additionally, our revolving credit facility contains various covenants and restrictive provisions which limit our and our subsidiaries&#8217; ability to incur additional indebtedness, guarantees and/or liens; consolidate, merge or transfer all or substantially all of our assets; make certain investments or restricted payments; modify certain material agreements; engage in certain types of transactions with affiliates; dispose of assets; and prepay certain i</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ndebtedness. If we fail to perform our obligations under these and other covenants, the revolving credit commitment could be terminated and any outstanding borrowings, together with accrued interest, under the revolving credit facility could be declared immediately due and payable. Our revolving credit facility also has cross default provisions that apply to any other indebtedness we may have with an outstanding principal amount in excess of $50 million. </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The revolving credit facility agreement contains certain negative covenants that (i)&#160;limit our ability, as well as the ability of certain of our subsidiaries, among other things, to enter into hedging arrangements and create liens and (ii)&#160;require us to maintain a consolidated leverage ratio, and an EBITDA </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">to interest expense ratio, in each case as described in the credit facility agreement. The revolving credit facility agreement also provides for the discontinuance of the requirement for us to maintain the EBITDA to interest expense ratio and allows for us to release all collateral securing the revolving credit facility if we reach investment grade status. The revolving credit facility agreement also requires us to maintain a consolidated leverage ratio of 5.5 to 1.0 (or 5.0 to 1.0 after we have released all collateral upon achieving investment grade status). We were in compliance with all covenants under the agreement at December&#160;31, 2013. </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Senior Notes.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%"><a name="_cp_text_1_441"></a>On April&#160;19, </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2011, we and ACMP Finance Corp. a wholly owned subsidiary of Access MLP Operating, L.L.C.,<a name="_cp_text_1_450"></a> completed a private placement of $350.0 million in aggregate principal amount of 5.875 percent senior notes due 2021 ( the &#8220;2021 Notes&#8221;).
