</table></div><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The carrying amount of cash and cash equivalents, accounts receivable and accounts payable reported on the balance sheet approximates fair value. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Segments</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">.&#160;</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Prior to the CMO Acquisition, the Partnership&#8217;s operations were organized into a single business segment. As a result of the CMO Acquisition, the Partnership added in three new operating regions. Effective January 1, 2013, the Partnership&#8217;s chief operating decision maker began to measure performance and allocate resources based on geographic segments. The Partnership&#8217;s operations are divided into eight operating segments: Barnett Shale, Eagle Ford Shale, Haynesville Shale, Marcellus Shale, Niobrara Shale, Utica Shale, Mid-Continent region and Corporate.</font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Revenue Recognition</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">. In 2013, the Partnership derived the majority of its revenues through gas gathering agreements with Chesapeake and Total. Pursuant to their respective applicable gas gathering a</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">greements, Chesapeake and Total have agreed to minimum volume commitments covering production in the Barnett Shale region for each year through December&#160;31, 2018 and for the six month period ending June&#160;30, 2019, and, solely with respect to Chesapeake, in the Haynesville Shale region for each year through December&#160;31, 2013 and December&#160;31, 2017 for the Springridge and Mansfield systems, respectively. In the event either Chesapeake or Total does not meet its minimum volume commitment to the Partnership in the Barnett Shale region or Chesapeake does not meet its minimum volume commitment to the Partnership in the Haynesville Shale region, for any annual period (or six month period with respect to the six months ending June&#160;30, 2019 in the Barnett Shale region) during the minimum volume commitment period, Chesapeake and Total will be obligated to pay a fee equal to the applicable fee for each Mcf by which the applicable party&#8217;s minimum volume commitment for such year (or six month period with respect to the six months ending June&#160;30, 2019) exceeds the actual volumes gathered from such party&#8217;s production. The revenue associated with such shortfall fees is recognized in the fourth quarter of each year. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Revenues consist of fees recognized for the gathering, treating, compression and processing of natural gas. Revenues are recognized when the service is performed and is based upon non-regulated rates and the related gathering, treating, compression and processing volumes. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Deferred Loan Costs. </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">External costs incurred</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> in connection with closing the revolving bank credit facilities are capitalized as deferred loan costs and amortized over the life of the related agreement. Amortization is included in interest expense in the statement of operations. </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">79</font></p>

<div style="width:100%;"><hr style="page-break-after:always"></div><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ACCESS MIDSTREAM PARTNERS, L.P. </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:4pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (continued)</font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Environmental Expenditures. </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Liabilities for loss contingencies, including environmental remediation costs, arising from claims, assessments, litigation, fines, and penalties and other sources are charged to expense when it is probable that a liability has been incurred and the amount of the assessment and/or remediation can be reasonably estimated. There are no liabilities reflected in the accompanying financial statements at December&#160;31, 2013 and 2012. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:2.67%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Equity Based Compensation</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">. Certain employees of the Partnership&#8217;s general</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> partner receive equity-based compensation through the Partnership&#8217;s equity-based compensation programs. The fair value of the awards issued is determined based on the fair market value of the shares on the date of grant. This value is amortized over the vesting period, which is generally four years from the date of grant. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:2.67%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Certain key members of management have been designated as participants in the Management Incentive Compensation Plan which is made up of two components. The first component is an annual cash bonus based on &#8220;excess&#8221; cash distributions made by the Partnership above a specified target amount with respect to each fiscal quarter during which the award is outstanding. The second component is based on an increase in value of the Partnership&#8217;s co</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">mmon units at the end of a specified five-year period beginning on the award commencement date. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:2.67%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Included in operating expense, general and administrative expense, and income from unconsolidated affiliates is total equity-based compensation of $35.0</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> million, $9.0 million and $3.8 million for the Partnership during the years ended December&#160;31, 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:2.67%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The LTIP provides for an aggregate of 3.5&#160;million common units to be awarded to employees, directors and consultants of the Partnership&#8217;s general partner and its affiliates through various award types, including unit awards, restricted units, phantom units, unit options, unit appreciation rights and other unit-based awards. The LTIP has been designed to promote the interests of the Pa</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">rtnership and its unitholders by strengthening its ability to attract, retain and motivate qualified individuals to serve as employees, directors and consultants. As of December&#160;31, 2013, there was $33.5 million of unrecognized compensation expense attributable to the LTIP, of which $29.7 million is expected to be recognized over a four year period. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:2.67%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The following table summarizes LTIP award activity for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">: </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:2.67%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;"><font style="font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</font></p><div>

</table></div><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:2.67%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Intangible Assets. </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Intangible assets are generally amortized on a straight-line basis over their estimated useful lives, unless the assets economic benefits are consumed on an other than straight-line basis. The estimated useful life is the period over which the assets are e</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">xpected to contribute directly or indirectly to the Partnership&#8217;s future cash flows. The estimated useful life of the customer relationship acquired with the Springridge gathering system and Appalachia Midstream is 15 years and 20 years for the CMO Acquisition. As of December 31, 2013, the carrying value of the Partnership&#8217;s intangible assets was $418.4 million, net of $46.0 of accumulated amortization.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Partnership estimates that it will record $22.8 million of intangible asset amortization for each of the next five years.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2012, the carrying value of the Partnership&#8217;s intangible assets was $377.8 million, net of $22.6 million of accumulated amortization.&nbsp;&nbsp;Amortization expense was $24.0 milllion, $11.3 million and $11.3 million for the years ended December&#160;31, 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively, for the Partnership. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:2.67%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The Partnership assesses long-lived assets, including property, plant and equipment and intangible assets, for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset may not be recoverable. Recoverability is assessed by comparing the carrying amount of an asset to undiscounted future net cash flows expected to be generated by the asset. If such assets are considered to be impaire</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">d, the impairment to be recognized is measured as the amount by which the carrying amounts exceed the fair value of the assets. </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">80</font></p>

<div style="width:100%;"><hr style="page-break-after:always"></div><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ACCESS MIDSTREAM PARTNERS, L.P. </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:4pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (continued)</font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Business Combinations. </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The Partnership makes various assumptions in developing models for determining the fair values of assets</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> and liabilities associated with business acquisitions. These fair value models, developed with the assistance of outside consultants, apply discounted cash flow approaches to expected future operating results, considering expected growth rates, development opportunities, and future pricing assumptions to arrive at an economic value for the business acquired. The Partnership then determines the fair value of the tangible assets based on estimates of replacement costs less obsolescence. Identifiable intangible assets acquired consist primarily of customer contracts, customer relationships, trade names, and licenses and permits. The Partnership values customer relationships using a discounted cash flow model. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Income taxes</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">. As a master limited partnership, the</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> Partnership is a pass-through entity and also not subject to federal income taxes and most state income taxes with the exception of Texas Franchise Tax. For federal and state income tax purposes, all income, expenses, gains, losses and tax credits generate flow through to the owners, and accordingly, do not result in a provision for income taxes. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Variable Interest Entities (VIEs). </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">An entity is referred to as a VIE pursuant to accounting guidance for consolidation if it possesses one of the following crite</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ria: (i)&#160;it is thinly capitalized, (ii)&#160;the residual equity holders do not control the entity, (iii)&#160;the equity holders are shielded from the economic losses, (iv)&#160;the equity holders do not participate fully in the entity&#8217;s residual economics, or (v)&#160;the entity was established with non-substantive voting interests. We consolidate a VIE when we have both the power to direct the activities that most significantly impact the activities of the VIE and the right to receive benefits or the obligation to absorb losses of the entity that could be potentially significant to the VIE. We continually monitor both consolidated and unconsolidated VIEs to determine if any events have occurred that could cause the primary beneficiary to change. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;margin-left:4.54%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:-4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold;;font-size:10pt;;">&nbsp;</p><div align="left"><table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%"><tr><td valign="top" style="width:4.54%;white-space:nowrap"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">3.</font></p></td><td valign="top" style="width:95.46%;"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Partnership Distributions </font></p></td></tr></table></div><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The partnership agreement requires that, within 45&#160;days subsequent to the end of each quarter, the Partnership distributes all of its available cash (as defined in the partnership agreement) to unitholders of record on the applicable record date. During the years ended December&#160;31, 2013, 2012 and 2011, the Partnership paid cash distributions to its unitholders of approximately $</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">389.1 million, $251.7 million and $200.9&#160;million, respectively, representing the four quarterly distributions in 2013, 2012 and 2011. See also Note&#160;14&#160;&#8212; Subsequent Events concerning distributions approved in January 2014 for the quarter ended December&#160;31, 2013. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Available cash</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">. The amount of available cash (as defined in the partnership agreement) generally is all cash on hand at the end of the quarter less the amount of cash reserves established by the Partnership&#8217;s general partner to provide for the proper conduct of its busi</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ness, including reserves to fund future capital expenditures, to comply with applicable laws, or its debt instruments and other agreements, or to provide funds for distributions to its unitholders and to its general partner for any one or more of the next four quarters. Working capital borrowings generally include borrowings made under a credit facility or similar financing arrangement. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Conversion of Subordinated Units.</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%"> Upon payment of the cash distribution for the second quarter of 2013, the subordination</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> period with respect to the Partnership&#8217;s 69,076,122 subordinated units expired and all outstanding subordinated units converted into common units on a one-for-one basis on August&#160;15, 2013. The conversion did not impact the amount of the cash distribution paid or the total number of the Partnership&#8217;s outstanding units representing limited partner interests. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Class B Units. </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The Class B units are not entitled to cash distributions. Instead, prior to conversion into common units, the Class B units receive quar</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">terly distributions of additional paid-in-kind Class B units. The amount of each quarterly distribution per Class B unit is the quotient of the quarterly distribution paid to the Partnership&#8217;s common units by the volume-weighted average price of the common units for the 30-day period prior to the declaration of the quarterly distribution to common units. Effective on the business day after the record date for the distribution on common units for the fiscal quarter ending December&#160;31, 2014, each Class B unit will become convertible at the election of either the Partnership or the holders of such Class B unit into a common unit on a one-for-one basis. In the event of the Partnership&#8217;s liquidation, the holders of Class B units will be entitled to receive out of the Partnership&#8217;s assets available for distribution to the partners the positive balance in each such holder&#8217;s capital account in respect of such Class B units, determined after allocating the Partnership&#8217;s net income or net loss among the partners. All Class B units are held indirectly by affiliates of the Partnership&#8217;s general partner. The Class B units were issued at a discount to the market price of the common units which they are convertible. This discount totaling $58.3 million represents a beneficial conversion </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">81</font></p>

<div style="width:100%;"><hr style="page-break-after:always"></div><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ACCESS MIDSTREAM PARTNERS, L.P. </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:4pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (continued)</font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">feature and is reflected as an increase in common unitholders&#8217; capital and a decrease in Class B units capital to reflect the fair value of the Class B units at issuance on the Partnership&#8217;s consolidated statement of changes in partners&#8217; capital for the twelve months ended December&#160;31, 2012. The beneficial conversion feature is considered a non-cash distribution recognized ratably from the issuance date of December&#160;20, 2012, through the conversion date, resulting in an increase in Class B units capital and a decrease in common unitholders&#8217; capital. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Class C Units. </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The Class C units </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">were entitled to quarterly cash distributions after the common units received the minimum quarterly distribution, plus any arrearages from prior quarters. The Class C units participated pro rata thereafter and received the minimum quarterly distribution, after which the Class C units participated in further cash distributions pro rata with the Partnership&#8217;s common units. Effective on the business day after the record date for the distribution on common units for the fiscal quarter ending December&#160;31, 2013, each Class C unit became convertible at the election of either the Partnership or the holders of such Class C unit into a common unit on a one-for-one basis. In the event of the Partnership&#8217;s liquidation, the holders of Class C units were entitled to receive out of the Partnership&#8217;s assets available for distribution to its partners the positive balance in each such holder&#8217;s capital account in respect of such Class C units, determined after allocating the Partnership&#8217;s net income or net loss among the Partners. All Class C units were held indirectly by affiliates of the Partnership&#8217;s general partner. The Class C units were issued at a discount to the market price of the common units which they are convertible. This discount totaling $36.7 million represents a beneficial conversion feature and is reflected as an increase in common unitholders&#8217; capital and a decrease in Class C units capital to reflect the fair value of the Class C units at issuance on the Partnership&#8217;s consolidated statement of changes in partners&#8217; capital for the twelve months ended December&#160;31, 2012. The beneficial conversion feature is considered a non-cash distribution recognized ratably from the issuance date of December&#160;20, 2012, through the conversion date, resulting in an increase in Class C units capital and a decrease in common unitholders&#8217; capital. Effective February 19, 2014, all of the Class C units converted into common units on a one-for-one basis. Please read Note 14 (Subsequent Events).&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">General Partner Interest and Incentive Distribution Rights</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">. The Partnership&#8217;s general partner is entitled to</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> two percent of all quarterly distributions that the Partnership makes prior to its liquidation. The general partner has the right, but not the obligation, to contribute a proportionate amount of capital to the Partnership to maintain its current general partner interest. The general partner&#8217;s initial two percent interest in the Partnership&#8217;s distributions may be reduced if the Partnership issues additional limited partner units in the future (other than the issuance of common units upon conversion of outstanding Class B or the issuance of common units upon a reset of the incentive distribution rights) and its general partner does not contribute a proportionate amount of capital to the Partnership to maintain its two percent general partner interest. After distributing amounts equal to the minimum quarterly distribution to common unitholders (and Class B unitholders, upon conversion of Class B units to common units) and distributing amounts to eliminate any arrearages to common unitholders, the Partnership&#8217;s general partner is entitled to incentive distributions if the amount the Partnership distributes with respect to any quarter exceeds specified target levels shown below: </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;"><font style="font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</font></p><div>

The maximum distribution sharing percentage of 50.0 percent includes distributions paid to the general partner on its two percent general partner interest and does not include any distributions that the general partner may receive on limited partner units that it owns or may </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">acquire. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;margin-left:4.54%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:-4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold;;font-size:10pt;;">&nbsp;</p><div align="left"><table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; The allocation of undistributed earnings, or net income in excess of distributions, to the incentive distribution </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">82</font></p>

<div style="width:100%;"><hr style="page-break-after:always"></div><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ACCESS MIDSTREAM PARTNERS, L.P. </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:4pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (continued)</font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">rights is limited to available cash (as defined by the partnership agreement) for the period. The Partnership&#8217;s net income allocable to the limited partners is allocated between the common, subordinated, Class B and Class C unitholders by applying the provisions of the partnership agreement that govern actual cash distributions as if all earnings for the period had been distributed. Accordingly, if current net income allocable to the limited partners is less than the minimum quarterly distribution, or if cumulative net income allocable to the limited partners since August&#160;3, 2010 is less than the cumulative minimum quarterly distributions, more income is allocated to the common unitholders than the subordinated, Class B and Class C unitholders for that quarterly period. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Basic and diluted net income per limited partner unit is calculated by dividing the limited partners&#8217; interest in net income by the weighted average number of limited partner units outstanding during the period. The common units issued during the period are included on a weighted-average basis for the days in which they were outstanding. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The following table illustrates the Partnership&#8217;s calculation of net income per unit for common and subordinated limited partner units (in thousands, except per-unit information): </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;"><font style="font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</font></p><div>

however, Mr.&#160;Dell&#8217;Osso, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Chesapeake, remained on the Partnership&#8217;s board of directors. The Partnership does not expect to complete additional significant transactions with Chesapeake. While Mr.&#160;Dell&#8217;Osso remains on the Partnership&#8217;s board, the Partnership no longer considers Chesapeake to be an affiliate of Access Midstream Partners. Because Chesapeake was the Partnership&#8217;s affiliate for a portion of 2012, set forth below is a description of the Partnership&#8217;s transactions with Chesapeake prior to 2013. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Affiliate transactions. </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">In the normal course of business, natural gas gathering, treating and other midstream services </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">were provided to Chesapeake and its affiliates. Revenues were derived primarily from Chesapeake, which included volumes attributable to third-party interest owners that participated in Chesapeake&#8217;s operated wells. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Omnibus Agreement. </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The Partnership entered into an omnibus agreement with Access Midstream Ventures an</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">d Chesapeake Midstream Holdings that addressed the Partnership&#8217;s right to indemnification for certain liabilities and its obligation to indemnify Access Midstream Ventures and affiliated parties for certain liabilities. </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">83</font></p>

<div style="width:100%;"><hr style="page-break-after:always"></div><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ACCESS MIDSTREAM PARTNERS, L.P. </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:4pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (continued)</font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">General and Administrative Services and Reimbursement</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">. Pursuant to a services agreement, Chesapeake and its affiliates provided certain services including legal, accounting, treasury, human resources, information technology and administration. The employees supporting these operations were employees of Chesapeake Energy Marketing Inc. (&#8220;CEMI&#8221;) or Chesapeake. The consolidated financial statements for the Partnership and the predecessor included costs allocated from Chesapeake and CEMI for centralized general and administrative services, as well as depreciation of assets utilized by Chesapeake&#8217;s centralized general and administrative functions. Effective October&#160;1, 2009, the Partnership was charged a general and administrative fee from Chesapeake based on the terms of the joint venture agreement. The established terms indicated corporate overhead costs were charged to the Partnership based on actual cost of the services provided, subject to a fee per Mcf cap based on volumes of natural gas gathered. The fee was calculated as the lesser of $0.0310/Mcf gathered or actual corporate overhead costs. General and administrative charges were $22.3 million and $23.7 million for the years ended December&#160;31, 2012 and 2011 for the Partnership. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Additional Services and Reimbursement</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">. At the Partnership&#8217;s req</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">uest, Chesapeake also provided the Partnership with certain additional services under the services agreement, including engineering, construction, procurement, business analysis, commercial, cartographic and other similar services to the extent they were not already provided by the seconded employees. In return for such additional services, the general partner reimbursed Chesapeake on a monthly basis an amount equal to the time and materials actually spent in performing the additional services. The reimbursement for additional services was not subject to the general and administrative services reimbursement cap. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Chesapeake agreed to perform all services under the relevant provisions of the services agreement using at least the same level of care, quality, timeliness and skill as it </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">did for itself and its affiliates and with no less than the same degree of care, quality, timeliness and skill as its past practice in performing the services for itself and the Partnership&#8217;s business during the one year period prior to September&#160;30, 2009. In any event, Chesapeake agreed to perform such services using no less than a reasonable level of care in accordance with industry standards. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">In connection with the services arrangement, the Partnership reimburses GIP for certain costs incurred by GIP in connection with assisting the Partnersh</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ip in the operation of its business. The cost for these support services was $0.4 million, $1.7 million, and $0.6 million for the years ended December&#160;31, 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Employee Secondment Agreement</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">. Chesapeake, certain of its affiliates and the Partnership&#8217;s general partner entered into an amended and restated employee secondment agreement pursuant to which specified employees of Chesapeake </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">were seconded to the general partner and provided operating, routine maintenance and other services with respect to the Partnership&#8217;s business under the direction, supervision and control of the general partner. Additionally, all of the Partnership&#8217;s executive officers other than its chief executive officer, Mr.&#160;Stice, were seconded to the general partner pursuant to this agreement. The general partner, subject to specified exceptions and limitations, reimbursed Chesapeake on a monthly basis for substantially all costs and expenses Chesapeake incurred relating to such seconded employees, including the cost of their salaries, bonuses and employee benefits, including 401(k), restricted stock grants and health insurance and certain severance benefits. Charges to the Partnership for the services rendered by such seconded employees were $49.4 million and $42.1 million for the years ended December&#160;31, 2012 and 2011, respectively. These charges included $37.7 million and $37.7 million in operating expenses and $11.7 million and $4.4 million in general and administrative expenses for the years end December&#160;31, 2012 and 2011, respectively, in the accompanying consolidated statements of operations. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Shared Services Agreement. </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">In return for the services of Mr.&#160;Stice as the c</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">hief executive officer of the Partnership&#8217;s general partner during the years ended December 2012 and 2011, its general partner entered into a shared services agreement with Chesapeake pursuant to which its general partner reimbursed certain of the costs and expenses incurred by Chesapeake in connection with Mr.&#160;Stice&#8217;s employment. The general partner was generally expected, subject to certain exceptions, to reimburse Chesapeake for 50 percent of the costs and expenses of the amounts provided to Mr.&#160;Stice in his employment agreement; however, the ultimate reimbursement obligation was determined based on the amount of time Mr.&#160;Stice actually spent working for the Partnership. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Gas Compressor Master Rental and Servicing Agreement</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">. The Partnership </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">has entered into a gas compressor master rental and servicing agreement with MidCon Compression, L.L.C., (&#8220;MidCon Compression&#8221;) a wholly owned indirect subsidiary of Chesapeake, pursuant to which MidCon Compression agreed to provide the Partnership certain compression equipment that the Partnership uses to compress gas gathered on its gathering systems outside the Marcellus Shale and provide certain related services. In return for providing such equipment, the Partnership pays specified monthly rates per specified compression units, subject to an annual escalator to be applied on October&#160;1st of </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">84</font></p>

<div style="width:100%;"><hr style="page-break-after:always"></div><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ACCESS MIDSTREAM PARTNERS, L.P. </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:4pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (continued)</font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">each year and a redetermination of such specified monthly rates to market rates effective no later than October&#160;1, 2016. Under the compression agreement, the Partnership granted MidCon Compression the exclusive right to provide compression equipment to the Partnership in the acreage dedications through September&#160;30, 2016. Thereafter, the Partnership will have the right to continue receiving such equipment through September&#160;30, 2019 at market rates to be agreed upon between the parties or to receive compression equipment from unaffiliated third parties. MidCon Compression guarantees to the Partnership that the compressors will meet specified run time and throughput performance guarantees. The monthly rates are reduced for any equipment that does not meet these guarantees.&nbsp;&nbsp;The compression agreement expires on September&#160;30, 2019 but will continue from year to year thereafter, unless terminated by the Partnership no less than 60 days prior to the end of the term or any year thereafter. The Partnership receives substantially all of the compression capacity for its existing gathering systems in the Marcellus Shale from MidCon Compression under a long-term contract expiring on January&#160;31, 2021 pursuant to which the Partnership has agreed to pay specified monthly rates under a fixed-fee structure subject to an annual escalator. This agreement is not subject to an exclusivity provision. Compressor charges from affiliates were $65.3 million and $57.6 million for the years ended December&#160;31, 2012 and 2011, respectively. These charges are included in operating expenses in the accompanying consolidated statements of operations. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The Partnership is obligated to maintain general liability and property insurance, including machinery breakdown insurance with respect to the equipment. In addition, MidCon Compression has agreed to provide the Partnership with emission testing and other related services at monthly rates. The Partnership or MidCon Compression may terminate these services upon not less than six months notice.</font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;margin-left:4.54%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:-4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold;;font-size:10pt;;">&nbsp;</p><div align="left"><table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%"><tr><td valign="top" style="width:4.54%;white-space:nowrap"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">6.</font></p></td><td valign="top" style="width:95.46%;"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Concentration of Credit Risk </font></p></td></tr></table></div><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Chesapeake is the only customer from whom revenues exceeded 10 percent of consolidated revenues for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013 for the Partnership. </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Chesapeake and Total are the only customers from whom revenues exceeded 10 percent of consolidated revenues for the years ended December&#160;31, 2012 and 2011 for the Partnership. The fair values of the gathering assets, related equipment, and intangible assets acquired were based on the market, cost and income approaches. All fair-value measurements of assets acquired and liabilities assumed are based on inputs that are not observable in the market and thus represent Level 3 inputs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Upon completion of the initial purchase price allocation, the Partnership reviewed its assessment, including the identification and fair valuation of assets acquired and liabilities assumed.&nbsp;&nbsp;During the third quarter 2013, the Partnership finalized certain of the estimates used in the initial purchase price allocation, primarily with respect to the valuation of assets and liabilities assumed in the Marcellus region.&nbsp;&nbsp;The balance sheet has been prospectively adjusted to reflect these changes, the most significant of which included a decrease to property, plant and equipment of $70.8 million, an increase to intangible assets of $55.4 million and an increase to other net assets of $15.4 million. None of the adjustments impacted the partnership&#8217;s statements of operations. </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">86</font></p>

<div style="width:100%;"><hr style="page-break-after:always"></div><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ACCESS MIDSTREAM PARTNERS, L.P. </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:4pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (continued)</font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Marcellus</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">. On December&#160;29, 2011, the Partnership acquired from CMD all of the</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> issued and outstanding common units of Appalachia Midstream for total consideration of $879.3 million, consisting of 9,791,605 common units and $600.0 million in cash that was financed with a draw on the Partnership&#8217;s revolving credit facility. The base purchase price of $879.3 million was increased by $7.3 million due to initial working capital adjustments through December&#160;31, 2011. Through the acquisition of Appalachia Midstream, the Partnership operates 100 percent of and owns an approximate average 47 percent interest in 10 gas gathering systems that consist of approximately 549 miles of gas gathering pipeline in the Marcellus Shale. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The results of operations presented and discussed in this annual report include results of operations from the Appalachia Midstream for the full year of operations in 2012 and the </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">three-day period from closing of the acquisition on December&#160;29, 2011, through December&#160;31, 2011. The Partnership&#8217;s interest in the gas gathering systems is accounted for as an equity investment and is included in income from unconsolidated affiliate. For the three-day period ended December 31, 2011, income from unconsolidated affiliate attributable to Marcellus operations was $0.4 million. The purchase price in excess of the value underlying the gas gathering system assets and working capital is approximately $461.2 million and is attributable to customer relationships acquired. This intangible asset is being amortized over a 15 year period on a straight-line basis. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The following table presents the pro forma condensed financial information of the Partnership as if the CMO</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> Acquisition and our acquisition of Appalachia Midstream each occurred on January&#160;1, 2011. The pro forma adjustments reflected in the pro forma condensed consolidated financial statements are based upon currently available information and certain assumptions and estimates; therefore, the actual effects of these transactions will differ from the pro forma adjustments. However, the Partnership&#8217;s management considers the applied estimates and assumptions to provide a reasonable basis for the presentation of the significant effects of certain transactions that are expected to have a continuing impact on the Partnership. In addition, the Partnership&#8217;s management considers the pro forma adjustments to be factually supportable and to appropriately represent the expected impact of items that are directly attributable to the transfer of CMO and Appalachia Midstream to the Partnership. </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;"><font style="font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</font></p><div>

(&#8220;Mid-Atlantic&#8221;) to Chesapeake for net proceeds of $32.9</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> million.&nbsp;&nbsp;Mid-Atlantic was acquired by the Partnership in December 2012 as part of the CMO Acquisition and consisted of midstream assets in the Marcellus Shale region.&nbsp;&nbsp;These assets were not part of the Partnership&#8217;s equity investment in Appalachia Midstream.&nbsp;&nbsp;The net proceeds equaled the Partnership&#8217;s basis in the assets. </table></div><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Marcellus</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">. On December&#160;29, 2011, the Partnership acquired from CMD, a wholly owned subsidiary of Chesapeake, and certain of its affiliates, all of the issued and outstanding common units of Appalachia Midstream </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">for approximately $879.3 million. Through the acquisition of Appalachia Midstream, the Partnership operates 100 percent of and owns an approximate average 47 percent interest in 10 gas gathering systems that consist of approximately 549 miles of gas gathering pipeline in the Marcellus Shale in Pennsylvania and West Virginia. These 10 gathering systems consist of the Liberty, Victory, Rome and Selbyville gas gathering systems and six other smaller gas gathering systems. The remaining 53 percent interest in these assets is owned primarily by Statoil, Anadarko, Epsilon and Mitsui. Appalachia Midstream operates the assets under 15-year fixed fee gathering agreements. The 10 gathering systems are separate investments with varying ownership percentages and each gathering system is accounted for as an equity investment because all capital expenditures and other operating decisions must be approved by a supermajority vote of the gathering system&#8217;s owners. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Utica East Ohio Midstream, LLC.</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%"> </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Partnership acquired UEOM as part of the CMO Acquisition in December 2012. In March 2012, CMO entered into an agreement to form Utica East Ohio Midstream LLC (&#8220;UEOM&#8221;) with M3 Midstream, L.L.C. and EV Energy Partners, L.P. to develop necessary infrastructure for the gathering, processing and fractionation of natural gas and NGLs in the Utica Shale play in Eastern Ohio. The infrastructure complex, which is currently under construction, consists of natural gas gathering and compression facilities constructed and operated by the Partnership, as well as processing, NGL fractionation, loading and terminal facilities constructed and operated by M3 Midstream, L.L.C. The Partnership owns a 49 percent interest and UEOM is accounted for as an equity investment because the power to direct the activities which are most significant to UEOM&#8217;s economic performance is shared between the Partnership and the other equity holders. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Ranch Westex JV, LLC.</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%"> </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Partnership acquired Ranch Westex as part of the CMO Acquisition in December 2012. On December&#160;1, 2011, CMO entered into a joint venture to form Ranch Westex JV, LLC. (&#8220;Ranch Westex&#8221;) with Regency Energy Partners, LP and Anadarko Pecos Midstream LLC to build a processing facility in Ward County, Texas, to process natural gas delivered from the liquids-rich Bone Springs and Avalon Shale formations. The Partnership owns a 33.33 percent interest and Ranch Westex is accounted for as an equity method investment because the power to direct the activities that are most significant to Ranch Westex&#8217;s economic performance is shared among the three equity holders. The project consists of two plants, a refrigeration plant and a cryogenic processing plant.  </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">88</font></p>
