</table></div><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Revolving Credit Facility. </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On May 13, 2013, the Partnership amended its existing senior secured revolving credit facility. The amended and restated revolving credit facility matures in May 2018 and includes revolving commitments of $1.75 billion, including a sub-limit of $100 million for same-day swing line advances and a sublimit of $200 million for letters of credit. In addition, the revolving credit facility&#8217;s accordion feature allows the Partnership to increase the available borrowing capacity under the facility up to $2.0 billion, subject to the satisfaction of certain conditions, including the identification of lenders or proposed lenders that agree to satisfy the increased commitment amounts under the revolving credit facility.</font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Borrowings under the revolving credit facility are available to fund working capital, finance capital expenditures and acquisitions, provide for the issuance of letters of credit and for general partnership purposes. The revolving credit facility is secure</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">d by all of the Partnership&#8217;s assets, and loans thereunder (other than swing line loans) bear interest at the Partnership&#8217;s option at either (i)&#160;the greater of (a)&#160;the reference rate of Wells Fargo Bank, NA, (b)&#160;the federal funds effective rate plus 0.50 percent or (c)&#160;the Eurodollar rate which is based on the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR), plus 1.00 percent, each of which is subject to a margin that varies from 0.50 percent to 1.50 percent per annum, according to the Partnership&#8217;s leverage ratio (as defined in the agreement), or (ii)&#160;the Eurodollar rate plus a margin that varies from 1.50 percent to 2.50 percent per annum, according to the Partnership&#8217;s leverage ratio. If the Partnership reaches investment grade status, the Partnership will have the option to release the security under the credit facility and amounts borrowed will bear interest under a specified ratings-based pricing grid. The unused portion of the credit facility is subject to commitment fees of (a)&#160;0.25 percent to 0.375 percent per annum while the Partnership is subject to the leverage-based pricing grid, according to the Partnership&#8217;s leverage ratio and (b)&#160;0.15 percent to 0.30 percent per annum while the Partnership is subject to the ratings-based pricing grid, according to its senior unsecured long-term debt ratings. </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Additionally, the revolving credit facility contains various covenants and restrictive provisions which limit the Partnership and its subsidiaries&#8217; ability to incur additional indebtedness, guarantees and/or liens; consolidate, merge or transfer all or substantially all of the Partnership&#8217;s assets; make certain investments or restricted payments; modify certain material agreements; engage in certain types of transactions with affiliates; dispose of assets; and prepay </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">certain indebtedness. If the Partnership fails to perform its obligations under these and other covenants, the revolving credit commitment could be terminated and any outstanding borrowings, together with accrued interest, under the revolving credit facility could be declared immediately due and payable. The revolving credit facility also has cross default provisions that apply to any other indebtedness the Partnership may have with an outstanding principal amount in excess of $15 million.</font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The revolving credit facility agreement contains certain negative covenants that (i)&#160;limit the Partnership&#8217;s ability, as well as the ability of certain of its subsidiaries, among other things, to enter into hedging arrangements and create liens and (ii)&#160;require the Partner</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ship to maintain a consolidated leverage ratio, and an EBITDA to interest expense ratio, in each case as described in the credit facility agreement. The revolving credit facility agreement also provides for the discontinuance of the requirement for the Partnership to maintain the EBITDA to interest expense ratio and allows for the Partnership to release all collateral securing the revolving credit facility if the Partnership reaches investment grade status. The revolving credit facility agreement also requires the Partnership to maintain a consolidated leverage ratio of 5.5 to 1.0 (or 5.0 to 1.0 after the Partnership has released all collateral upon achieving investment grade status). The Partnership was in compliance with all covenants under the agreement at December 31, 2013.</font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">90</font></p>

<div style="width:100%;"><hr style="page-break-after:always"></div><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ACCESS MIDSTREAM PARTNERS, L.P. </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:4pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (continued)</font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Senior Notes</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">. On December&#160;19, 2012, the Partnership and ACMP Finance Corp., a wholly owned subsidiary of Access MLP Operating, L.L.C., completed a public offering of $1.4 billion in aggregate principal amount of 4.875 percent senior notes due 2023 (the &#8220;2023 Notes&#8221;). The Partnership used a portion of the net proceeds to fund a portion of the purchase price for the CMO Acquisition, and the balance to repay borrowings outstanding under the Partnership&#8217;s revolving credit facility. Debt issuance costs of $25.9 million are being amortized over the life of the 2023 Notes. </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">On January&#160;11, 2012, the Partnership and ACMP Finance Corp. completed a private placement of $750.0 million in aggregate principal amount of 6.125 percent senior notes due 2022 (the &#8220;2022 Notes&#8221;). The Partnership used a portion of the net proceeds to repay all borrowings outstanding under its revolving credit facility and used the balance for general partnership purposes. Debt issuance costs of $13.8 million</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> are being amortized over the life of the 2022 Notes. </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">On April&#160;19, 2011, the Partnership and ACMP Finance Corp. completed a private placement of $350.0 million in aggregate principal amount of 5.875 percent senior notes due 2021 ( the &#8220;2021 Notes&#8221;). The Partnership used a portion of the net proceeds to repay borrowings outstanding under its revolving credit facility and used the balance for general partnership purposes. Debt issuance costs of $8.2 million are being amortized over the life of the 2021 Notes</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">. </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">On August 14, 2013, the Partnership issued $400</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> million in aggregate principal amount of additional 5.875 percent senior notes due 2021 (the &#8220;Additional Notes&#8221;). The Additional Notes are additional to the $350 million of 2021 Notes initially issued on April 19, 2011 and are fully fungible with, rank equally with and form a single series with the 2021 Notes.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Additional Notes were issued at a price of 101.5 percent of the principal amount plus accrued interest from April 15, 2013, resulting in net proceeds of $400.8 million, which was used for general partnership purposes, including funding working capital, repayment of indebtedness and funding the Partnership&#8217;s capital expenditure program.&nbsp;&nbsp;Debt issuance costs of $5.8 million are being amortized over the life of the Additional Notes.</font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The 2023 Notes will mature on May&#160;15, 2023, and interest is payable on May&#160;15 and November&#160;15 of each year. The Partnership has the option to redeem all or a portion of the 2023 Notes at any time on or after December&#160;15, 2017, at the redemption price specified in the indenture relating to the 2023 Notes, plus accrued and unpaid interest. The Partnership may also redeem the 2023 Notes, in whole or in part, at a &#8220;make-whole&#8221; redemption price specified in the indenture, plus a</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ccrued and unpaid interest, at any time prior to&#160;December 15, 2017. In addition, the Partnership may redeem up to 35 percent of the 2023 Notes prior to December&#160;15, 2015 under certain circumstances with the net cash proceeds from certain equity offerings. </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The 2022 Notes will mature on July&#160;15, 2022 and interest is payable on January&#160;15 and July&#160;15 of each year. The Partnership has the option to redeem all or a portion of the 2022 Notes at any time on or after January&#160;15, 2017, at the redemption price specified in the indenture relating to the 2022 Notes, plus accrued and unpaid interest. The Partnership may also redeem the 2022 Notes, in whole or in part, at a &#8220;make-whole&#8221; redemption price specified in the indenture, plus accrued and unpaid interest, at any</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> time prior to&#160;January 15, 2017. The Partnership has the option to redeem all or a portion of the 2021 Notes at any time on or after April&#160;15, 2015, at the redemptio</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">n price specified in the indenture, plus accrued and unpaid interest. The Partnership may also redeem the 2021 Notes, in whole or in part, at a &#8220;make-whole&#8221; redemption price specified in the indenture, plus accrued and unpaid interest, at any time prior to&#160;April 15, 2015. In addition, the Partnership may redeem up to 35 percent of the 2021 Notes prior to April&#160;15, 2014 under certain circumstances with the net cash proceeds from certain equity offerings. </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The 2023 Notes, 2022 Notes and the 2021 Notes indentures contain covenants that, among other things, limit the Partnership&#8217;s ability and the ability of certain of the Partnership&#8217;s subsidiaries to: (1)&#160;sell assets including equity interests in its subsidiaries; (2)&#160;pay distributions on, redeem or purchase th</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">e Partnership&#8217;s units, or redeem or purchase the Partnership&#8217;s subordinated debt; (3)&#160;make investments; (4)&#160;incur or guarantee additional indebtedness or issue preferred units; (5)&#160;create or incur certain liens; (6)&#160;enter into agreements that restrict distributions or other payments from certain subsidiaries to the Partnership; (7)&#160;consolidate, merge or transfer all or substantially all of the Partnership&#8217;s or certain of the Partnership&#8217;s subsidiaries&#8217; assets; (8)&#160;engage in transactions with affiliates; and (9)&#160;create unrestricted subsidiaries. These covenants are subject to important exceptions and qualifications. If the 2023 Notes, 2022 Notes or the 2021 Notes </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">91</font></p>

The guarantees are full and unconditional and joint and several, subject to certain automatic customary releases, including sale, disposition, or transfer of the capital stock or substantially all of the assets of a subsidiary guarantor, exercise of legal defeasance option or covenant defeasance option, and designation of a subsidiary guarantor as unrestricted in accordance with the applicable indenture. There are no significant restrictions on the ability of the Partnership or any guarantor to obtain funds from its subsidiaries by dividend or loan. None of the assets of the Partnership or a guarantor represent restricted net assets pursuant to Rule 4-08(e)(3) of Regulation S-X under the Securities Act. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%"> </font><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Capitalized Interest. </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Interest expense was net of capitalized interest of $43.9 million, $14.6 million, and $9.5 million for the years ended December&#160;31, 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively, for the Partnership. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;margin-left:4.54%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:-4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold;;font-size:10pt;;">&nbsp;</p><div align="left"><table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; <div style="width:100%;"><hr style="page-break-after:always"></div><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:4pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">PART III </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;margin-left:10.27%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:-10.27%;font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold;;font-size:10pt;;">&nbsp;</p><div align="left"><table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%"><tr><td valign="top" style="width:10.27%;white-space:nowrap"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ITEM&#160; 10.</font></p></td><td valign="top" style="width:89.73%;"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="Directors"></a></font><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Directors, Executive Officers and Corporate Governance</font><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> </font></p></td></tr></table></div><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management of the Partnership </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">As a limited partnership, we have no directors or officers. Instead, Access Midstream Partners GP, L.L.C., our general partner, manages our operations and activities. Our general partner is not elected by our unitholders and will not be subject to re-election in the future. Our general partner owes a fiduciary duty to our unitholders. Our general partner is liable, as a general partner, for all of our debts (to the extent not paid from our assets), except for indebtedness or other obligations that are made </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">specifically nonrecourse to it. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The directors of our general partner oversee our operations. Access Midstream Ventures, which is jointly and equally owned by the GIP II Entities and Williams, is the sole member of our general partner and has the right to appoint our general partner&#8217;s entire board of directors. Unitholders are not entitled to elect the directors of our general partner or directly or indirectly participate in our management or operations, and the GIP II Entities and Williams have agreed betw</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">een themselves as to how and when replacement, removals and appointments of directors may be made. Our general partner currently has 13 directors: Alan S. Armstrong, Donald R. Chappel, James E. Scheel, James J. Cleary, William A. Woodburn, William J. Brilliant, J. Mike Stice, Robert S. Purgason, Dominic J. Dell&#8217;Osso, Jr., David A. Daberko, Philip L. Frederickson, Suedeen G. Kelly and William B. Berry. Our general partner&#8217;s board of directors has affirmatively determined that David A. Daberko, William B. Berry, Philip L. Frederickson and Suedeen G. Kelly satisfy the NYSE and SEC requirements for independence for directors. The NYSE does not require a listed publicly traded partnership, like us, to have a majority of independent directors on our general partner&#8217;s board of directors or to establish a compensation committee or a nominating/corporate governance committee, although our general partner&#8217;s board of directors has established an audit committee, a conflicts committee, a compensation committee and a risk committee. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The officers of our general partner manage and conduct our operations. In 2013, all of the executive officers of our general partner devoted all of their time to manage and conduct our operations.</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.53%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Directors and Executive Officers </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The following table shows information regarding the current executive officers and directors of our general partner. Directors are appointed for a term of one year. The directors hold office until their successors have been duly elected and qualified or until th</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">e earlier of their death, resignation, removal or disqualification. Officers serve at the discretion of the board of directors. There are no family relationships among any of our general partner&#8217;s directors or executive officers. </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;"><font style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</font></p><div>

The board has determined that each member of the audit committee is independent under the NYSE listing standards and the Exchange Act. The audit committee held eight meetings in 2013. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Mr.&#160;Daberko has been designated by our general partner&#8217;s board of directors as an</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> &#8220;audit committee financial expert&#8221; meeting the requirements promulgated by the SEC, based upon his education and employment experience as more fully detailed in Mr.&#160;Daberko&#8217;s biography set forth above. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The audit committee assists the board of directors in its oversight of the integrity of our financial statements and our compliance with legal and regulatory requirements and Partnership policies and controls. The audit committee has the sole authority to, among other things, (i)&#160;retain and terminate our independent registered public accou</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">nting firm, (ii)&#160;approve all auditing services and related fees and the terms thereof performed by our independent registered public accounting firm and (iii)&#160;establish policies and procedures for the pre-approval of all non-audit services and tax services to be rendered by our independent registered public accounting firm. The audit committee is also responsible for confirming the independence and objectivity of our independent registered public accounting firm. Our independent registered public accounting firm has been given unrestricted access to the audit committee and our management, as necessary. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Conflicts Committee</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">. The conflicts committee consists of three independent members of our general partner&#8217;s board of directors, Messrs. Daberko and Frederickson and Ms.&#160;Kelly. Mr.&#160;Frederickson is the current chairman of the conflicts committee. The conflicts committee review</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">s specific matters that the board believes may involve conflicts of interest (including certain transactions with Chesapeake historically, GIP, Williams and/or Access Midstream Ventures) and which it determines to submit to the conflicts committee for review. The conflicts committee determines if the resolution of the conflict of interest is fair and reasonable to us. The members of the conflicts committee may not be officers or employees of our general partner or directors, officers or employees of its affiliates, including Williams, GIP and/or Access Midstream Ventures, and must meet the independence and experience standards established by the NYSE and the Exchange Act to serve on an audit committee of a board of directors, along with other requirements in our partnership agreement. Any matters approved by the conflicts committee will be conclusively deemed to be fair and reasonable to us, approved by all of our partners and not a breach by our general partner of any duties it may owe us or our unitholders. The conflicts committee held two meetings in 2013. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Compensation Committee</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">. Harris effective March 14, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Mr. Harris was replaced as the chariman by Mr. Woodburn effective October 24, 2013. Mr.&#160;Woodburn is the current chairman of the compensation committee. The objectives of the compensation committee are to develop an executive compensation system that is competitive with the Partnership&#8217;s peers and encourages both short-term and long-term performance in a manner beneficial to the Partnership and its operations. In fulfilling this objective, the compensation committee oversees compensation decisions for the officers of our general partner and administers our Long Term Incentive Plan with respect to the officers of our general partner, selecting individuals to be granted equity-based awards from among those eligible to participate. The compensation committee has </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">102</font></p>

Significant risks and the possible approaches to mitigate such risks are reviewed by the risk committee at periodic meetings and presented to the board&#8217;s risk management director to assess the impact on our strategic objectives and risk tolerance levels. Ms.&#160;Kelly currently serves as the board&#8217;s risk management director and updates the board on a quarterly basis regarding any risk management developments. In addition, the audit committee is responsible for overseeing the Partnership&#8217;s financial risks. Shiels, Purgason, Bennett and Seldenrust based on their respective employment agreements as well as a comprehensive, subjective evaluation of the Partnership&#8217;s performance and their individual performances. The compensation committee of the board of directors of our general partner reviews and approves the total compensation for the named executive officers. Awards to the named executive officers under our Long-Term Incentive Plan (&#8220;LTIP&#8221;) and Management Incentive Compensation Plan (&#8220;MICP&#8221;) are also expressly approved by the board of directors of our general partner. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.53%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Elements and Mix of Compensation </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">We provided short-term compensation in the form of base salaries, </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">cash bonuses, long-term compensation in the form of equity awards and 401(k) matching contributions and certain perquisites. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.53%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cash Salary and Bonuses </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The base salary levels of the named executive officers are intended to reflect each named executive officer&#8217;s base level of responsibility, leadership, tenure and contribution to the success and profitability of the organization. Base salaries tend to be less variable over ti</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">me and are intended to contribute less to total compensation than incentive awards. Messrs. Shiels&#8217;, Bennett&#8217;s and Seldenrust&#8217;s base salaries increased $15,000, $35,000 and $16,000, respectively, during 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Messrs. Stice&#8217;s and Purgason&#8217;s base salaries did not increase in 2013. Cash bonuses paid during 2013 were intended to provide incentives based on a subjective performance assessment over a shorter period of time than the equity compensation listed below.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our named executive officers&#8217; cash bonuses were determined by the compensation committee of the board of directors of our general partner in its discretion, based on its subjective assessment of our performance and our named executive officers&#8217; performance over the first half of calendar year 2013 and over the second half of calendar year 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Mr. Bennett was paid $75,000 of his 2013 annual bonus on January 18, 2013, and $85,000 of his 2013 annual bonus on July 19, 2013. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.53%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Equity-Based Compensation </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The equity-based compensation of the named executive officers was intended to provide incentives for long-term performance that increases unitholder value by aligning the interests of the unitholders and the named executive officers. </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">106</font></p>

<div style="width:100%;"><hr style="page-break-after:always"></div><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:4pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Equity awards were granted to the named executive officers in January and July as part of Access&#8217;s semi-annual review of employee compensation.&nbsp;&nbsp;Mr. Bennett received an equity unit award valued at $105,000 on January 2, 2013, and an equity unit award valued at $300,000 on July 10, 2013. Each of Messrs. Stice, Purgason, Shiels, Bennett and Seldenrust received phantom unit awards under our LTIP, which is described below under &#8220;Long-Term Incentive Plan&#8221;. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.53%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management Incentive Compensation Plan </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Our general partner maintains the amended and restated MICP, providing incentive </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">compensation awards consisting of two components, to key members of management who have been designated as participants by our general partner. Mr.&#160;Stice was granted an MICP award in December 2012 and Messrs. Shiels and Purgason were each granted MICP awards in December 2012 and January 2010.&nbsp;&nbsp;No MICP awards were granted to our named executive officers in 2013. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The first component of each award is an annual cash bonus based on &#8220;excess&#8221; cash distributions made by us above a specified target amount with respect to each fiscal quarter during which the award is outstanding, beginning with the fiscal quarter in which the grant date occurs (the &#8220;Excess Return Component&#8221;). A participant&#8217;s Excess Return Component will generally be calculated by multiplying the &#8220;exc</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ess&#8221; distribution amount for an applicable quarter (the amount of distributions that were made over &#8220;target&#8221; for that quarter) by the participant&#8217;s participation percentage assigned to him at the time of grant, by the annual payment percentage that is set forth in the MICP (unless otherwise assigned to the participant at the time of the grant). The Excess Return Component determined to be payable to a participant with respect to the quarters within a specified fiscal year (if any) is paid in annual installments over the first five years following the award commencement date, provided the participant continues to be employed by us or an affiliate until the payment date. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The second component is based on an increase in value of our common units at the end of a specified five-year period beginning on the award commencement date and is measured and paid at the end of such period (the &#8220;Equity Uplift Component&#8221;), unless a change of control occurs prior to the expiration of the period, at which time the award would </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">be paid upon that change of control, as described in more detail below under &#8220;Potential Payments Upon Termination or Change of Control.&#8221; The Equity Uplift Component is calculated by multiplying the &#8220;equity uplift value,&#8221; if any, by the participants &#8220;equity uplift value percentage.&#8221; The &#8220;equity uplift value&#8221; is defined as the excess of the value of our units on the payment date over the value of our units on a date specified at the time of grant ($25.07 for the 2012 awards and $21.00 for the 2010 awards), multiplied by the number of our outstanding units on the payment date. Each participant&#8217;s &#8220;equity uplift value percentage&#8221; is assigned pursuant to an award agreement. Awards that may become due under the Equity Uplift Component may be paid in the form of a single lump sum in cash or common units, at the discretion of the board of directors of our general partner. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Certain payments may become due to MICP participants upon a &#8220;qualified termination&#8221; or a &#8220;change of control&#8221; (as those terms are defined in the MICP). For additional information, see &#8220;Potential Payments Upon Termination or Change of Control&#8221; below. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Other Compensation Arrangements </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Access also provided compensation in the form of personal benefits and perquisites to the named executive officers in 2013. Most of the benefits that Access provided to the named executive officers are the same benefits that are provided to all employees or large groups of senior-level employees of Access, including health and welfare insurance benefits, 401(k) benefits, wh</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ich include matching contributions (up to 12 percent of an employee&#8217;s annual base salary and cash incentive bonus compensation).&nbsp;&nbsp;Access does not have a pension plan or any other retirement plan other than the 401(k) and retirement restoration plans.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:4.54%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Employment Agreements </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Each of the named executive officers is a party to an employment agreement with our general partner that became effective January 1, 2013, that governs the terms and conditions of their employment, including their duties and responsibilities, compensation and benefits, and applicable severance terms, which are described below under &#8220;Potential Payments Upon Termination or Change of Control.&#8221; The employment agreements are each described below. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:4.54%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Employment Agreement with J. Mike Stice </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Mr.&#160;Stice&#8217;s employment agreement became effective January&#160;1, 2013 and has an initial employment term ending on June&#160;30, 2017, subject to automatic one-year renewals thereafter. Pursuant to the agreement, Mr.&#160;Stice will serve as the Chief Executive Officer of our general partner, with an initial annual base salary of $750,000, subject to review and </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">107</font></p>

<div style="width:100%;"><hr style="page-break-after:always"></div><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:4pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">increase by our general partner&#8217;s Board in its discretion. During the term of his employment, Mr.&#160;Stice is also eligible to participate in the employee benefit plans and arrangements, such as retirement, health and welfare plans and vacation programs that are customarily provided to similarly situated executives of our general partner, in accordance with the terms and conditions of such plans and arrangements.<a name="_cp_text_1_282"></a> In addition, during his term of employment, our general partner may, in its discretion, pay annual or periodic bonus compensation to Mr. Stice from time to time, subject to the requirement that Mr. Stice be employed by our general partner on the bonus payment date. Frederickson</font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Long-Term Incentive Plan </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:4.54%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">General </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Our general partner has adopted the Access Midstream LTIP, for employees, consultants and directors of our general partner and its affiliates, who perform services for us. The summary of the LTIP contained herein does not purport to be complete and is qualified in its entirety by reference to the LTIP. The LTIP provides for the grant of unit awards, restricted units, phantom units, unit options, unit appreciation rights, distribution equivalent rights with respect to phantom units, and other unit-based awar</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ds. Subject to adjustment for certain events, an aggregate of 3,500,000 common units may be delivered pursuant to awards under the LTIP. Units from awards that are cancelled or forfeited are available for delivery pursuant to other awards. The LTIP is administered by our general partner&#8217;s board of directors. The LTIP has been designed to promote the interests of the Partnership and its unitholders by strengthening the Partnership&#8217;s ability to attract, retain and motivate qualified individuals to serve as directors, consultants and employees. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:4.54%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Restricted Units and Phantom Units </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">A restricted unit is a common unit that is subject to forfeiture during the restricted period. Upon vesting, the forfeiture restrictions lapse and the recipient holds a common unit that is not subject to forfeiture. A phantom unit is a notional unit that entitles the grantee to receive a common unit upon the vesting of the phantom unit or, in the discretion of our general partner, cash equal to the fair market value of a common unit. T</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">he board of directors of our general partner may make grants of restricted units and phantom units under the LTIP that contain such terms, consistent with the LTIP, as the board may determine are appropriate, including the period over which restricted or phantom units will vest. Our general partner may, in its discretion, base vesting on the grantee&#8217;s completion of a period of service or upon the achievement of specified financial objectives or other criteria or upon a change of control (as defined in the LTIP) or as otherwise described in an award agreement. Upon the vesting of phantom units, common units equal to the number of phantom units then vesting, or cash equal to the fair market value thereof, is delivered to the grantee, less the number of units or amount of cash equal to the income taxes payable on the vesting of the phantom units. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Distributions made by us with respect to awards of phantom units may, in the discretion of the board of directors of our general partner, be subject to the same vesting requirements as the restricted units. Our general partner, in its discretion, may also grant tandem distribution equivalent rights with respect to phantom units. Distribution equivalent rights are rights to receive an amount equal to all or a portion of </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">the cash distributions made on units during the period a phantom unit remains &#8220;outstanding.&#8221; Restricted units and phantom units granted under the LTIP serve as a means of incentive compensation for performance and not primarily as an opportunity to participate in the equity appreciation of the common units. Therefore, participants do not pay any consideration for the common units they receive with respect to these types of awards, and neither we nor our general partner receives remuneration for the units delivered with respect to these awards. </font></p><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">109</font></p>

<div style="width:100%;"><hr style="page-break-after:always"></div><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:4pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:4.54%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Unit Options and Unit Appreciation Rights </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The LTIP also permits the grant of options and unit appreciation rights covering common units. Unit options represent the right to purchase a number of common units at a specified exercise price. Unit appreciation rights represent the right to receive the appreciation in the value of a number of common units over a specified exercise price, either in cash or in common units as determined by the board. Unit options and unit app</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">reciation rights may be granted to such eligible individuals and with such terms as our general partner may determine, consistent with the LTIP; however, a unit option or unit appreciation right must have an exercise price greater than or equal to the fair market value of a common unit on the date of grant. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Other Unit-Based Awards </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The LTIP also permits the grant of other unit-based awards, which are awards that, in whole or in part, are valued or based on or related to the value of a unit. The vesting of any other unit-based award may be based on a participant&#8217;s length of service, the achievement of performance criteria or other measures. On vesting, any other unit-based award may be paid in cash and/or in units (including restricted units), as our general</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> partner may determine. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Source of Common Units; Cost </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Common units to be delivered with respect to awards may be newly issued units, common units acquired by our general partner in the open market, common units already owned by our general partner or us, common units acquired by our general partner from any other person or any combination of the foregoing. Our general partner will be entitled to reimbursement by us for the cost incurred in acquiring such common units. If we issue new common units with resp</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ect to these awards, the total number of common units outstanding will increase, and our general partner will remit the proceeds it receives from a participant, if any, upon exercise of an award to us. With respect to any awards settled in cash, our general partner will be entitled to reimbursement by us for the amount of the cash settlement. With respect to unit options and unit appreciation rights, our general partner will be entitled to reimbursement from us for the difference between the cost it incurs in acquiring these common units and the proceeds it receives from an optionee at the time of exercise of an option. Thus, we will bear the cost of the unit options. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Amendment or Termination of Long-Term Incentive Plan </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The board of directors of our general partner, in its discretion, may terminate the LTIP at any time with respect to the common units for which a grant has not previously been made. The LTIP will automatically terminate on the earlier of the 10th anniversary of the date it was initially adop</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ted by our general partner or when common units are no longer available for delivery pursuant to awards under the LTIP. The board of directors of our general partner will also have the right to alter or amend the LTIP or any part of it from time to time or to amend any outstanding award made under the LTIP; provided, however, that no change in any outstanding award may be made that would materially impair the vested rights of the participant without the consent of the affected participant, and/or result in taxation to the participant under Section&#160;409A of the Internal Revenue Code (the &#8220;Code&#8221;). </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Upon a change of control of us or our general partner, the board of directors of our general partner may, in its sole discretion: </font></p><div align="left"><table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; The value realized on vesting is based on the closing price of the Partnership&#8217;s common units on the vesting dates. </font></p></td></tr></table></div><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">114</font></p>

<div style="width:100%;"><hr style="page-break-after:always"></div><p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:4pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:-0.01%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;">&nbsp;</p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Potential Payments Upon Termination or Change of Control </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.13%;font-family:Arial;"><a name="_cp_text_1_388"></a><font style="font-style:italic;;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.13%">Employment Agreements.</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.13%">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_cp_text_1_391"></a>As discussed under &#8220;Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#8221; above, each of the named executive officers is a party to an employment agreement with our general partner, each of which became effective January 1, 2013, that govern the terms and conditions of their employment, including their duties and responsibilities, compensation and benefits, and applicable severance terms.&nbsp;&nbsp;The energy industry&#8217;s history of terminating professionals during its cyclical downturns and the frequency of mergers, acquisitions and consolidation in our industry are two important factors that have contributed to a widespread, heightened concern for long-term job stability by many professionals in our industry.&nbsp;&nbsp;In response to this concern, arrangements that provide compensation guarantees in the event of an employee&#8217;s termination without cause, death or incapacity or due to a change of control are common pra<a name="_cp_text_1_393"></a>ctice in our industry. These provisions in the named executive officers&#8217; employment agreements and the incentive plans in which the named executive officers participated were integral to our ability to recruit and retain the high caliber of professionals t<a name="_cp_text_1_395"></a>hat are critical to the successful execution of our business strategy.&nbsp;&nbsp;Below is a discussion of the arrangements in effect during calendar year 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.13%;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-style:italic;;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.13%">J. Mike Stice Employment Agreement</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.13%"><a name="_cp_text_1_397"></a>. Mr. Stice's employment agreement </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">provides for certain change of control and termination benefits in the event of a<a name="_cp_text_1_400"></a> termination of Mr. Stice's employment under certain circumstances.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;"><a name="_cp_text_1_401"></a><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Upon <a name="_cp_text_1_403"></a>a </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">termination of his employment without &#8220;cause&#8221; or for a &#8220;good reason condition&#8221; (each <a name="_cp_text_1_405"></a>as defined in the employment <a name="_cp_text_1_406"></a>agreement), subject to his execution of a release<a name="_cp_text_1_408"></a>, Mr. Stice is entitled to <a name="_cp_text_1_409"></a>receive an amount equal to (i) 200% of his then-current annual base salary, plus (ii) any accrued but unused vacation as of the date of termination, payable in <a name="_cp_text_1_412"></a>a lump sum within thirty <a name="_cp_text_1_414"></a>days following termination. If such termination occurs within two years after a &#8220;<a name="_cp_text_1_416"></a>change of control&#8221; (as defined in the employment agreement), Mr. Stice is entitled to receive (in lieu of the severance benefits described above) an amount <a name="_cp_text_1_418"></a>equal to (a) 250% of the sum <a name="_cp_text_1_420"></a>of (i) his <a name="_cp_text_1_421"></a>then-current annual base salary and (ii) <a name="_cp_text_1_422"></a>the most recent <a name="_cp_text_1_423"></a>actual annual bonus (or, if the most recent annual bonus was paid semi-annually, the two most recent semi-annual <a name="_cp_text_1_424"></a>bonuses) paid to Mr. Stice during the twelve-month period preceding the cha<a name="_cp_text_1_426"></a>nge of control, plus (b) any accrued but unused vacation as of the date of termination, payable in a lump sum within thirty days following termination. </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%"><a name="_cp_text_1_428"></a>Upon a termination of </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_cp_text_1_430"></a>Mr. Stice&#8217;s employment due to his death or incapacity, subject (in the case of his incapacity) to the execution of a release<a name="_cp_text_1_432"></a>, Mr. Stice (or his estate, as applicable) is entitled to receive an amount equal to (i) 100% of his then-current annual base salary, plus (ii) any accrued but unused vacation as of the date of termination, payable in a lump sum following such termination. Upon any other termination of employment (including a termination for &#8220;cause&#8221; or due to the expiration or non-renewal of the employment term), Mr. Stice will be <a name="_cp_text_1_434"></a>entitled to receive only accrued but unpaid vacation <a name="_cp_text_1_437"></a>through the date of termination. Stice, Shiels and Purgason are participants in the MICP. Mr.&#160;Stice holds awards granted under the MICP in 2012, and Messrs. Shiels and Purgaso</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">n hold awards granted under the MICP in 2010 and 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the MICP, if a participant&#8217;s employment terminates for any reason prior to a payment date, other than due to (i)&#160;his death, disability, (ii)&#160;involuntary termination by the employer other than for &#8220;cause&#8221; (as defined in the MICP), or (iii)&#160;by the participant for a &#8220;good reason&#8221; (as defined in the MICP) (each such event in (i), (ii)&#160;and (iii), a &#8220;Qualified Termination&#8221;), then the participant&#8217;s award will be automatically forfeited on his or her termination of employment, to the extent then unpaid. If, however, a participant&#8217;s termination of employment prior to a payment date is a Qualified Termination, the participant will be paid (i)&#160;on his termination the remaining amount of any unpaid annual installments attributable to the participant&#8217;s Excess Return Component for the fiscal quarters that have been completed as of the participant&#8217;s termination date, and (ii)&#160;at the end of the applicable five-year period, (a) with respect to the 2012 MICP awards, the full amount of the participant&#8217;s Equity Uplift Component (if any) and (b) with respect to the 2010 MICP awards, a pro-rated amount of the participant&#8217;s Equity Uplift Component (if any) (in each case, except as otherwise described below in connection with a change of control). Pursuant to a December 2012 amendment to Mr.&#160;Purgason&#8217;s 2010 award under the MICP, a nonrenewal of his employment term under his new employment agreement with our general partner will also be treated as a Qualifying Termination under the MICP for purposes of his 2010 award. Awards will be paid in cash, unless the board of directors of our general partner otherwise elects, in its discretion, to pay all or part of the Equity Uplift Component of the award in our common units. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">Upon a change of control (as defined in the MICP), a participant who is an employee immediately prior to the change of control will be paid (i)&#160;with respect to the Excess Return Component, the remaining amount of unpaid annual installments attributable to fiscal quarters then completed and (ii)&#160;with respect to the Equity Uplift Component, an amount based on the increase in the value of our common units as of the change of control date over the value of our common </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">units at the award commencement date. A participant who has incurred a Qualified Termination prior to the change of control will receive, with respect to the Equity Uplift Component (instead of the amounts due under clause (ii)&#160;above), a pro rata portion of the amount that otherwise would have been payable to him had his employment continued until the change of control. The MICP will terminate on a change of control. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The tables below provide estimates of the compensation and benefits that would have been payable to Messrs. </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Stice, Shiels, Purgason, Bennett and Seldenrust under each the above described arrangements if such termination events had been triggered as of December&#160;31, 2013. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;;">&nbsp;</p><div>

Our independent directors receive compensation for their service on our general partner&#8217;s board of directors. Such compensation consists of an annual retainer of $80,000 for each board member, except for the chairman of the board of directors who receives $100,000. The independent directors</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> also receive an initial grant of the number of units having a grant date value of approximately $50,000 upon initial appointment as a director of our general partner. The independent directors also receive an annual grant, effective on the first business day of January of each year that they serve as a director, of the number of units having a grant date value of approximately $50,000, 25 percent of which will vest on the grant date and 75 percent of which will be phantom units that vest one-third on each of the first, second and third anniversary of the date of grant (with vesting to be accelerated upon death, disability or a change of control of our general partner). In addition, each director is reimbursed for out-of-pocket expenses in connection with attending meetings of the board of directors or committees. Each director is fully indemnified by us, pursuant to individual indemnification agreements and our partnership agreement, for actions associated with being a director to the fullest extent permitted under Delaware law. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">On January&#160;3, 2014</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">, each of Messrs. Daberko, Berry and Frederickson and Ms.&#160;Kelly was awarded 915 phantom units, 229 of which were immediately vested. </font></p><p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:4.54%">The following table sets forth the compensation earned by the directors of our general partner in 201</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">3: </font></p><p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0%;margin-right:0%;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;;"><font style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</font></p><div>
